ai_technology: Multilingual neural-network language models (including mBERT, XLM-R and NLLB); ridge-regression brain encoding

evidence.ai_role: Learned multilingual embeddings supply a common feature space for brain-response models and cross-language transfer tests.
evidence.tested: Cross-participant and held-out-language encoding on fMRI data; existing 12-language data and 27 new participants across nine languages. Reviewed v2 uses nested regularization and sequential validation with controls for temporal structure.
evidence.unknown: Fine-grained language differences and causality remain unresolved. Small cohorts and selection by response reliability constrain conclusions. The 2026 journal version was not reviewed in full.

organization: University of Milano-Bicocca; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Harvard University

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v2 archived full text through Europe PMC: language models, encoding design, participant selection, Results and limitations. Primary v1 metadata/abstract establishes earlier core result date; v2 Methods are not asserted identical to v1. Final 2026 Nature full text inaccessible.

summary: Multilingual neural-language-model embeddings enabled ridge-regression models of fMRI language-network responses that transferred to held-out languages across a 21-language study. The study combined existing data in 12 languages with newly collected data in nine more, supporting a shared representational component related to meaning. Small samples per language, reliability-based filtering and modest predictive correlations limit generalization; the results establish neither identical processing across languages nor a causal universal neural code. The core result was public in the February 2, 2025 preprint; the reviewed November 18, 2025 revision added analyses. A November 23, 2026 journal announcement is later source context, with final journal Methods not reviewed.
title: Multilingual model representations predict shared brain responses across languages
